_note: Computable extract of the Sierra Leone Integrated Obstetric and Newborn Care Guideline (MoHS, copy-edited version 19 Jan 2026). Only content Ovamha can evaluate from confirmed data is encoded. Every item cites its table or section. Thresholds the guideline does not state are marked 'assumption' and need MoHS confirmation. This file advises the health worker; the worker decides on referral.

referral_pathway._cite: Cross-cutting issues: Referral (minimum requirements; roles of the referring health worker); Antenatal care chapter: referral pathway for high-risk clients
referral_pathway.consent: Explain to the woman (and her family) the need for referral, the reason for the choice of facility, the expected cost and the possible outcome. Obtain informed consent.
emergency_checklist: Assess and stabilise her; maintain vital functions
Give pre-referral treatment for the specific condition
Be ready for an emergency delivery
A relative who can donate blood goes with her
If she is very ill, a health worker goes with her
Continue care and medication during referral
referral_pathway.call: Inform the call centre / referral coordinator using iSBAR (Identification, Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation) and alert the receiving facility.
referral_pathway.document: Complete the standard referral form; record the time of the call for the ambulance and the time it arrived.

management._note: Worker-facing management steps, transcribed from the guideline (it incorporates WHO ANC 2016 and WHO pre-eclampsia/eclampsia recommendations). Shown with the advice they belong to; never generated. The guideline's levels-of-care annex is not machine-readable, so every block carries the scope note.
management.scope_note: Do only what you are trained and supplied to do at your level of care.

blocks.title: Bleeding after 24 weeks (antepartum haemorrhage): initial resuscitation
blocks.cite: Obstetric complications: Antepartum haemorrhage (initial resuscitation and general management)
steps: SHOUT FOR HELP to urgently mobilise all available personnel.
Rapid evaluation of her general condition, then DR. ABC: Danger, Response, Airway, Breathing, Circulation. Check level of consciousness (AVPU).
Do NOT do a vaginal examination.
If shock is suspected, position her immediately and begin treatment; give a left lateral tilt.
Check the fetal heart rate and ask about fetal movements (below 110 or above 160 beats per minute: suspect fetal distress).
Send a blood sample for haemoglobin or haematocrit and type and screen (and order blood) before IV fluids; start an IV infusion and infuse IV fluids.

blocks.title: Severe pre-eclampsia / eclampsia: act fast, magnesium sulphate
blocks.cite: Pre-eclampsia and eclampsia: management; magnesium sulphate loading dose
steps: Respond as an emergency and work as a team. Magnesium sulphate (MgSO4) is the best anticonvulsant.
Loading dose (both): 4 g MgSO4 20% solution IV over 5-20 minutes (8 mL of 50% + 12 mL sterile water) AND 10 g MgSO4 50% IM: 5 g (10 mL) deep IM in each buttock, each with 1 mL lignocaine 2%.
If convulsions recur after 15 minutes: 2 g MgSO4 20% IV over 5 minutes (4 mL of 50% + 6 mL sterile water).
If advanced care will not be reached within 4 hours: first maintenance dose 5 g MgSO4 50% + 1 mL lignocaine 2% IM in one buttock, 4 hours after the loading dose.
Withhold MgSO4 if any toxicity sign: respiratory rate below 16 per minute, absent patellar reflexes, or urine output below 30 mL per hour over the preceding 4 hours.
Severe hypertension (BP 160/110 or above): hydralazine or labetalol may be used to control it.
If 24 to below 34 weeks and birth is expected within 7 days, with no suspected infection: dexamethasone 12 mg IM, repeat 12 mg IM after 24 hours.
Record on the MgSO4 monitoring sheet.

blocks.title: High risk of pre-eclampsia: prevention and monitoring
blocks.cite: Table 3.1 Antenatal care interventions (supplements); Table 3.2 Schedule of contacts; Pre-eclampsia and eclampsia: management
steps: Aspirin 75 mg daily (from after 12 weeks, as in the contact schedule).
Calcium 1.5-2.0 g oral elemental calcium daily (populations with low dietary calcium).
Check BP at every contact; if BP is raised, check urine for protein. Assess for danger signs.
If BP exceeds 140/90 mmHg, antihypertensive treatment may be initiated (labetalol, nifedipine or methyldopa are preferred in pregnancy).
Counsel: birth is recommended at 37 weeks for women with pre-eclampsia, at a facility able to do caesarean birth; educate her and her family about danger signs.
